newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TEICHMANN CONFIDENT ABOUT S.A. VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TEICHMANN CONFIDENT ABOUT S.A. VICTORY.

text.p: Springbok captain Gary Teichmann, while concerned that his side's preparations have been severely disrupted this week with the loss of three key backline players, remains confident that his men can level the test series against the Lions on Saturday.

In the last two days the South African side have lost through injury the services of experienced right winger James Small, powerful centre Japie Mulder and their frontline kicker in centre Edrich Lubbe.
Western Province wing Pieter Rossouw and Northern Transvaal centre Danie van Schalkwyk were then drafted into the squad as late replacements on Tuesday.

"Obviously these late withdrawals don't help us in preparing for what is really a crucial match. We are fully aware that we made a lot of mistakes in Cape Town and the Lions were quick to take advantage," Teichmann told Reuters.
"But I firmly believe we can bounce back and square the series here in Durban. We just have to keep calm and not let the pressure get to us as we did last year against the All Blacks.
"And we can't afford to be too negative about our Newlands defeat. There were some positives for us in that game and we must build on those."
Teichmann said his side had never underestimated the strength of the 1997 Lions."Although I think a lot of the South African media did," he added.

"But the only way you can prove them (our critics) wrong is on the field. Yesterday at Kings Park our practice was sharp. There were no mistakes and I think that shows that the pressure isn't getting to the guys."
South Africa's side for the second test against the Lions is to be announced in Durban at 12:30 p.m. (10:30 GMT) on Wednesday.

The entire Springbok pack from the first test in Cape Town is expected to be retained while the likely changes in the backline are Rossouw for Small, van Schalkwyk for Mulder and uncapped Western Province utility back Percy Montgomery for Lubbe (as both outside centre and first-choice kicker).

Likely S.A. team for Durban: Andre Joubert, Pieter Rossouw, Percy Montgomery, Danie van Schalkwyk, Andre Snyman, Henry Honiball, Joost van der Westhuizen, Gary Teichmann (captain), Andre Venter, Ruben Kruger, Hannes Strydom, Mark Andrews, Adrian Garve, Naka Drotske, Os du Randt.
